stem: Which sequence correctly shows the levels of organisation in a multicellular organism, from simplest to most complex?
options: Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism
Cell, organ, tissue, organ system, organism
Tissue, cell, organ, organism, organ system
Cell, tissue, organ system, organ, organism
explanation: Correct option: (A). Similar cells form a tissue, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems and organ systems form the organism. The other sequences place organ before tissue, tissue before cell, or organ system before organ.

stem: Why does the formation of different tissues help a multicellular organism?
options: It lets every cell perform all the functions of life equally.
It brings division of labour, raising the efficiency of the body.
It reduces the total number of cells the body needs to make.
It stops all the cells from dividing once the organism is fully formed.
explanation: Correct option: (B). Different tissues take up different jobs, which is division of labour and makes complex life processes efficient. A single cell doing everything describes unicellular organisms like amoeba; tissue formation neither reduces cell number nor stops all division.

stem: Plants are mostly fixed in one place, while most animals move about. Which difference in their cells best matches this?
options: Plant cells lack a nucleus; animal cells have a large nucleus for control.
Animal cells have a rigid cell wall that supports the body during movement.
Plant cells have a rigid cell wall; animal cells lack one and can change shape.
Plant cells are very flexible, so plants bend instead of needing to stay upright.
explanation: Correct option: (C). Fixed, upright plants need rigidity, which the cell wall gives, while the absence of a wall lets animal cells change shape, helping locomotion. Plant cells do have nuclei, animal cells do not have walls, and plant cells are not the flexible ones.

stem: Rohan says a tissue is a group of similar cells doing a similar job. For which example is his statement least accurate?
options: Parenchyma, built of living thin-walled cells that store food
Collenchyma, built of living cells with thickened corners
Sclerenchyma, built of thick-walled lignified dead cells
Phloem, built of sieve tubes, companion cells and fibres
explanation: Correct option: (D). Phloem is a complex tissue: several different cell types work together for one function, so 'similar cells' does not fit it well. Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are simple tissues made of one type of cell, where the statement holds.

stem: Which set of features is typical of meristematic cells?
options: Thick lignified walls, large vacuoles and very few organelles
Thin walls, large central vacuole, loosely packed cells
Thickened corners, small nucleus, many large air spaces
Thin walls, dense cytoplasm, prominent nucleus, no vacuoles

stem: A water plant floats easily even though its stem is soft. Which tissue feature best accounts for this?

Parenchyma with large air spaces between living cells
Collenchyma with pectin at the corners of the cells

stem: An elephant strips the bark of a tree all round the trunk, removing the phloem but not the wood. What is the most likely long-term effect?
options: Roots starve, as food from leaves can no longer reach them.
Leaves wilt at once, as water can no longer rise up to them.
The tree grows faster, as food now stays in the leaves.
Nothing changes, as phloem is made only of dead cells.
